prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a claim made by the executor of an estate. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the claimant is acting as executor or personal representative, I should pause for proof of authority before discussing cover in detail, because probate papers or equivalent confirmation often determine who can make the claim and receive settlement."},{"type":"fact","content":"When an estate claim is first reported, I should treat the contact as time-sensitive but avoid assuming the decedent’s policy still operates exactly as before, because occupancy, consent and use of the property may have changed."},{"type":"observation","content":"When there is no immediate occupier, I should ask early about property security, meter isolation and routine checks, because empty or partially empty homes are more vulnerable to escape of water, theft and avoidable deterioration."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the executor cannot answer every question straight away, I prefer to capture the basics, set a clear list of follow-up evidence and keep the claim moving, because estates often need time to gather documents and access the property."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the loss is storm or flood related, I should separate the damage caused by the insured event from pre-existing disrepair, because estate properties often have maintenance issues that affect the assessment of cover."},{"type":"fact","content":"When valuables, keepsakes or contents are involved, I should ask who has custody of the items and whether anything has already been distributed, because the executor may need to coordinate with beneficiaries before we can verify ownership and value."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the claim includes a vehicle, I should confirm whether the car is still being used, kept off-road or awaiting transfer, because the risk position changes once a registered keeper has died and administration is underway."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the executor is worried about delay, I prefer to explain what can be triaged within delegated authority and what must be escalated, because clear boundaries reduce frustration and prevent promises I cannot keep."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there may be multiple interested parties, I should keep my notes precise and neutral, because estate claims can involve executors, beneficiaries, solicitors and repairers, and inconsistent records slow settlement."},{"type":"observation","content":"When documents arrive piecemeal, I should re-check whether the policy schedule, death certificate, probate evidence and loss details all align, because estate claims often fail on missing links rather than on the merits of the loss."}]}
